newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank settles $29 million class action.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank settles $29 million class action.

text.p: NationsBank Corp said Friday it settled for $29 million a class action suit brought by investors who purchased investment products during 1993 and 1994 and alleged that they did not understand the risks.
NationsBank said it continues to deny the allegations but chose to resolve the matter so it could concentrate on its business.
Plaintiffs' attorneys will collect up to $10 million of the $29 million settement, NationsBank said.
NationsBank said the comprehensive agreement resolves all customer class-action claims against NationsSecurities.
At the time, NationsSecurities was a joint venture between NationsBank and Dean Witter. Dean Witter is now part of Morgan Stanley Dean Witter Discover & Co.

The joint venture was terminated in November, 1994 as the result of a business decision not related to the issues in the litigation. Dean Witter did not make any contribution to the $29 million settlement.

"We decided it was time to close the door and get back to our primary business, which is serving the investment needs of our customers," said John Munce, executive in charge of NationsBank's consumer business. He said the litigation could have continued another four to six years.

Munce said NationsSecurities in the period in question and continuing through the present has required customers to acknowledge their understanding of risk at the time of investments. He said the process has been enhanced with additional disclosures that give NationsBank "distinct proof" that the disclosures are adequate.
NationsSecurities is the third-largest bank-affiliated broker-dealer in the U.S. It has about 400 brokers and about 180,000 account relationships. The unit has $12 billion in assets under management.
Munce said an accounting provision was previously established to cover the cost of the settlement.
